ov: About 25 species of amphibious gobies that live on tropical mudflats and in mangroves, spending much of their time out of water. Their eyes sit on top of the head, and limb-like front fins let them crawl, skip across the mud and climb low branches.
rg: The Indo-Pacific and the Atlantic coast of Africa. One widespread species runs from East Africa and Madagascar to Southeast Asia, northern Australia, southern China and Samoa.
df: It varies by species: some eat detritus from the mud, others small crabs, insects, snails and even other mudskippers.
fx: It can leap up to 61 cm by flexing its body and pushing with its tail.
Males dig burrows in the mud, and some species keep an air pocket inside when the tide covers them.
